record.original_question: Let S_U = ∏_{i→U} S_n be the ultraproduct of symmetric groups with the normalized Hamming distance, viewed as a trace-preserving subgroup of the tracial matrix ultraproduct M_U = ∏_{n→U} M_n(C), and let W*(S_U) be the von Neumann algebra generated by S_U inside M_U. Does W*(S_U) contain a copy of a matrix ultraproduct?

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Denote by SU = ∏ i→U Sn, the ultraproduct of the symmetric groups with the normalized Hamming distance. Clearly, SU ⊂ MU in a trace preserving way ... Denote by W ∗(SU) the von Neumann subalgebra of MU generated by SU. Does W∗(SU) contain a copy of a matrix ultraproduct?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a free ultrafilter U on the natural numbers. For each n, let S_n denote the symmetric group on n letters, equipped with the normalized Hamming length ℓ(σ) = (1/n)·#{k : σ(k) ≠ k}, which yields the bi-invariant Hamming metric d(σ,τ) = ℓ(στ^{-1}). Embed S_n into the unitary group of the n×n complex matrix algebra M_n(C) via permutation matrices; equip M_n(C) with its normalized trace tr_n. Form the tracial matrix ultraproduct M_U = ∏_{n→U} M_n(C), a II_1 factor with trace τ((x_n)_n) = lim_{n→U} tr_n(x_n). The metric ultraproduct S_U = ∏_{i→U} S_n (defined as the quotient of the ℓ^∞-product by the normal subgroup of sequences with ℓ(σ_n) → 0 along U) embeds into the unitary group of M_U in a trace-preserving way through the permutation-matrix embedding. Let W*(S_U) ⊂ M_U denote the von Neumann subalgebra generated by S_U.

Question: Does W*(S_U) contain a unital subalgebra that is isomorphic to a tracial matrix ultraproduct ∏_{k→V} M_{n_k}(C) for some sequence n_k and some free ultrafilter V (in particular, a copy of the hyperfinite II_1 factor R^V realized as a matrix ultraproduct)?
